newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee firms on rising call rates.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee firms on rising call rates.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee gained on the back of rising money rates pushed up by increased government borrowings, dealers said.
The rupee was bid at 56.54 to the dollar at 0700 GMT, after opening at its previous closing level of 56.65, they said.
"High call money rates are keeping the dollar down as dealers swap to generate rupees," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer.
Call money had risen since the Central Bank took 1.1 billion rupees out of the system at last week's Treasury Bill auctions, dealers said.
Apart from extra money going out of the system, panic borrowing anticipating a rise in call money also contributed to the increase, they said.
Call money hit a high of 32 percent and a low of 26 in early trading, dealers said.
